title: How Rob Hallam learned to make good videos: seven lessons from a year of daily reps
summary: Rob Hallam argues video is the highest-leverage skill in 2026 and credits it for taking his business to $30,000 a month. He shares seven practical lessons from a year of daily videos: energy, viewer focus, intentional speaking, eye contact, hooks, audio, and captions. The unifying idea is deliberate reps and improving 1% each day.

principles.text: Video is a top-leverage skill; one good video reaches more people than you could ever meet.
principles.quote: One good video can reach more people than you could ever possibly meet in a single lifetime, and can open more doors and opportunities than you could even imagine.

principles.text: Getting good at video is about reps, not talent. Practice with intention, not randomly.
principles.quote: But, the reps have to be intentional and conscious. You have to be thinking, "Why am I doing this rep?"

principles.text: Make every video about the viewer: they are always asking how it helps them.
principles.quote: Whenever someone's watching a video online, they are thinking, "How is it helping me?"

principles.text: Value can be education, entertainment, or vulnerable storytelling, but not context-free talk about your day.
principles.quote: Entertainment is value. Education is value. Making a connection with someone by sharing a story vulnerably is value.

principles.text: Nail the hook: cover what they'll learn, the ROI of learning it, and why you're credible.
principles.quote: I made sure to tell you why I'm qualified to tell you. In other words, I'm not just some random guy who's never made a videos before.

principles.text: Add captions on social platforms since most people watch on mute; sound quality beats picture.
principles.quote: Approximately 75% of people online watch videos on mute.
